definition_en: to sit, lie or stand in a relaxed and lazy way; also a comfortable public room in a hotel, airport or house for waiting and relaxing

sceneCN: 这里 lounge 是名词「休息室、候机厅」（第 4 个义项：供等候休息的公共房间）；句意为我们陷进机场休息室的软椅，终于放松下来。画面里可认出休息区、行李和沙发。

senses.title: To sit or lie in a relaxed, lazy way
senses.definition: to sit, lean or lie somewhere in a comfortable and lazy way
senses.definitionCN: 以舒服而懒散的姿势坐、靠或躺在某处
senses.example: He lounged on the sofa all afternoon with the television on.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个下午都懒洋洋地靠在沙发上，开着电视。
senses.why: The word was first used of slow, languid movement, so the core image of sinking comfortably into a seat naturally becomes the verb for lazy resting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早描写缓慢而慵懒的动作，核心意象是舒服地陷进座位，由此自然长出表示懒散休息的动词义。

senses.title: To stand or move about in an idle way
senses.titleCN: 懒散地闲逛；无所事事地消磨时间
senses.definition: to spend time in a place standing, leaning or walking about without any purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在某个地方站着、倚着或随便走走，没有明确目的，消磨时间
senses.example: A few young men lounged by the gate, waiting for nothing in particular.
senses.exampleCN: 几个年轻人懒散地倚在大门边，也不特意等什么。
senses.why: If the body is too relaxed to act with purpose, resting in a seat widens into drifting about a place, so the same lazy posture gives the idle sense.
senses.whyCN: 当身体懒散到没有行动目标时，坐着休息就扩展成在某个地方闲荡，同一副慵懒姿态便衍生出无所事事的意思。

senses.title: A comfortable sitting room in a house
senses.definition: a room in a house where people sit and relax, especially in British English
senses.definitionCN: 住宅里供人坐下休息的房间，尤见于英式英语
senses.example: The family watched the match together in the lounge.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人在客厅里一起看比赛。
senses.why: The room got its name from what people do there: since to lounge is to relax lazily, the room set aside for lounging became the lounge.
senses.whyCN: 这个房间因人们在那里的动作而得名：既然 lounge 是懒散地休息，专门用来休息的房间就成了 the lounge。

senses.title: A comfortable room for waiting in a public place
senses.definition: a comfortable room at an airport, station, hotel or club where people can wait or relax
senses.definitionCN: 机场、车站、旅馆或俱乐部里供人等候、放松的舒适房间
senses.example: They waited for their flight in the business lounge.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在商务候机厅里等航班。
senses.why: Waiting used to be done standing in a hall; giving waiters a soft room where they can lounge comfortably extends the home sense to public buildings.
senses.whyCN: 过去人们等候时只能站在大厅里；给等候者一间可以懒散放松的软房间，就把家庭义延伸到了公共建筑里。

senses.title: A room or bar for drinking and socialising
senses.definition: a room in a hotel, club or bar, often with music, where people drink and talk
senses.definitionCN: 旅馆、俱乐部或酒吧里常配音乐的房间，供人喝酒、聊天
senses.example: The band played quiet jazz in the cocktail lounge.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在鸡尾酒廊里演奏轻柔的爵士乐。
senses.why: A room built for relaxing attracts drinks and conversation, so the waiting room sense drifts to the room where lounging happens over a drink.
senses.whyCN: 为放松而设的房间自然引来酒和聊天，于是等候室的意思偏向了那间一边喝一杯一边懒散度过的房间。

senses.title: A man's ordinary business suit
senses.definition: a man's usual matching jacket and trousers for business or formal daywear, in lounge suit
senses.definitionCN: lounge suit 里指男士平常穿的上衣西裤成套西服，用于商务或白天的正式场合
senses.example: The invitation asked gentlemen to wear a lounge suit.
senses.exampleCN: 请柬要求男士穿普通西服出席。
senses.why: Because a suit worn loosely at home was once contrasted with stiffer formal dress, the lazy word came to mark everyday formality rather than ease.
senses.whyCN: 由于在家松散穿用的西服曾与拘谨的礼服相对，这个表示懒散的词转而标记日常的正式装束，而不是指舒适本身。

senses.title: A man who idles in social places to impress others
senses.titleCN: 游手好闲的社交客（lounge lizard，旧式戏谑）
senses.definition: in the old informal phrase lounge lizard, a man who spends his time in lounges and hotels trying to impress people
senses.definitionCN: 旧式非正式说法 lounge lizard 里指常泡休息室与旅馆、装腔作势讨人喜欢的男人
senses.example: In the old novel, a lounge lizard occupied the hotel bar every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 在那本旧小说里，一个游手好闲的社交客每晚都占着旅馆酒吧。
senses.why: A person who only lounges about becomes a fixed type, so the lazy verb combines with a comic image to name the idle social climber.
senses.whyCN: 只会闲荡的人固化为一种人物类型，表示懒散的动词与滑稽意象组合，就用来称呼无所事事的社交客。

senses.title: Soft, relaxed popular music
senses.titleCN: 轻音乐风格的 lounge music
senses.definition: in lounge music, a style of quiet, easy-listening popular music played in bars and lounges
senses.definitionCN: lounge music 里指酒吧、酒廊常放的舒缓、放松的轻音乐风格

intro.en: The origin of lounge is uncertain; it first appears in sixteenth-century English as a verb for lazy, slow movement, and several explanations compete.
intro.cn: lounge 的来源不确定；它最早见于十六世纪英语，作动词表示缓慢慵懒的动作，目前并存几种解释。

items.en: The verb lounge appears in the sixteenth century meaning to move or act lazily and slowly; no earlier ancestor is securely recorded.
items.cn: 动词 lounge 在十六世纪出现，意为懒散、缓慢地行动；没有可靠的更早祖先形式被记录下来。

items.en: A common suggestion links it to the older word lungis, meaning a slow, lazy person; this connection is generally held but not proven.
items.cn: 一种常见看法把它与更早的 lungis（慢性子、懒人）联系起来；这一关联被普遍接受但未获证实。

items.en: Some treat lounge as an expressive or imitative coinage for languid movement, like several other lazy-motion verbs; this remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 也有人认为 lounge 是表达慵懒动作的拟声性造词，与其他几个表示懒散动作的动词相仿；这仍只是假说。

items.en: From the lazy action came a place where one lounges: by the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the noun named a place to lounge, and later a room for it.
items.cn: 由懒散动作引申出可以懒散的场所：十六至十七世纪名词开始指可供闲躺的地方，后来指专门的房间。

items.en: Modern English keeps both sides: the verb for lazy resting and wandering, and the noun for sitting rooms, airport lounges, bars and soft music.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了两个方向：动词表示懒散休息与闲荡，名词表示客厅、机场候机厅、酒吧与轻音乐风格。

definition_zh: 爱好者；恋人；情人；热爱者
definition_en: a person who loves someone romantically; also a person who greatly enjoys a particular activity or subject
core_image: 一个人把一束花轻轻放进另一双手里，目光只停在对方脸上
scene: 黄昏的街角，一个人把写好的信折好，塞进对方家的门缝，随后快步走开。The lover waited by the fountain every evening, holding a small red box.
sceneCN: 这里 lover 是「恋人、情人」（第 2 个义项：恋爱对象）；句意为恋人每晚都等在喷泉边，手里拿着一个小红盒。画面里可认出街角、折好的信与喷泉。

pos.zh: 爱好者；恋人；情人；热爱者

derivatives.zh: 构成 lover 的名词基础，义为「爱；爱情」
由 love 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可爱的；美好的」
由 love 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「惹人喜爱的」

senses.title: A person who greatly enjoys an activity or subject
senses.definition: a person who takes great interest and pleasure in a particular activity, subject or object
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动、学科或事物有浓厚兴趣并从中获得乐趣的人
senses.example: She is a lifelong music lover who never misses a concert.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一辈子的音乐爱好者，从不错过任何一场音乐会。
senses.why: The verb love means to hold something dear, and the person suffix -er turns that feeling into an identity, so anyone who loves a thing deeply can be called its lover.
senses.whyCN: 动词 love 表示珍视某物，表示「人」的后缀 -er 把这种感情变成一种身份，所以任何深爱某事物的人都可以被称为它的 lover。

senses.title: A person someone is in a romantic relationship with
senses.definition: a person with whom someone has a romantic and usually sexual relationship
senses.definitionCN: 与某人处于恋爱关系、通常也包含性关系的人
senses.example: He wrote a letter to his lover before leaving the city.
senses.exampleCN: 离开这座城市之前，他给恋人写了一封信。
senses.why: Romantic love is the most intense form of holding someone dear, so the same person suffix naturally names the one who receives that love rather than the one who only feels it.
senses.whyCN: 恋爱是「珍视某人」最强烈的一种形式，于是同一个表示人的后缀自然指接受这份爱的那个人，而不只是付出爱的人。

senses.title: A person in a secret or extramarital sexual relationship
senses.definition: a person who has a sexual relationship with someone who is married to another person or already has a partner
senses.definitionCN: 与已婚者或已有伴侣者保持性关系的人；婚外情人
senses.example: The novel opens with a married man meeting his lover in a small hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 小说一开头，一个已婚男子在一家小旅馆与情人见面。
senses.why: Because the romantic sense is strong, the word takes on a discreet and often disapproving colour when the relationship has to be hidden from a spouse.
senses.whyCN: 因为恋爱义很强烈，当这种关系必须对配偶隐瞒时，这个词就带上隐秘、常含贬义的色彩，用来指婚外情人。

intro.en: Lover is love plus the person suffix -er; love itself goes back to an Old English word for deep affection.
intro.cn: lover 是 love 加表示「人」的后缀 -er；love 本身可追溯到古英语中表示深厚感情的词。

items.en: Old English lufu named love as a feeling, and the verb lufian meant to love or to hold dear.
items.cn: 古英语 lufu 指「爱」这种感情，动词 lufian 意为爱、珍视。

items.en: The reconstructed ancestor is lubō, a form rebuilt by comparing related Germanic languages rather than found in writing.
items.cn: 其重构祖形为 lubō，这一形式是通过比较相关日耳曼语言重建出来的，并非见于书面记录。

items.en: Middle English joined love with -er and produced lover, a person who loves or is loved.
items.cn: 中古英语把 love 与 -er 结合，造出 lover，指爱着别人或被爱的人。

items.en: The word covered both the devoted admirer of an art and the partner in a romance, and context decided which one was meant.
items.cn: 这个词同时指对某门艺术痴迷的爱好者和恋爱中的伴侣，具体指哪一个由上下文决定。

items.en: Modern English keeps the romantic sense at the centre, while compounds such as music lover and nature lover preserve the older sense of devoted admirer.
items.cn: 现代英语以恋爱义为中心，而 music lover、nature lover 这类复合词保留了「痴迷的爱好者」这一较早含义。

note.cn: 形近组收 love 词族及其派生形式；近义组收其他表示爱慕、欣赏或被爱的人称。

entries.definition: A person one loves romantically; an affectionate form of address.
entries.definitionCN: 所爱的恋人；也用作亲昵称呼。

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent build from love and the person suffix -er, so its hooks come from the feeling, the suffix and the compounds it forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 love 与表示人的后缀 -er 清楚构成，记忆钩子来自这份感情、这个后缀以及它组成的复合词。

normal.en: Lover is love plus -er, so the word literally means the one who loves.
normal.cn: lover 是 love 加 -er，字面意思就是「爱的那个人」。

normal.en: The plural is lovers, made by adding s to the singular.
normal.cn: 复数是 lovers，直接在单数后加 s。

normal.en: Music lover and nature lover are fixed compounds that keep the sense of devoted admirer.
normal.cn: music lover 与 nature lover 是固定复合词，保留了「痴迷的爱好者」这层意思。

normal.en: Beloved adds the prefix be- to loved, giving the sense of being greatly loved.
normal.cn: beloved 在 loved 前加前缀 be-，表示「深受爱戴的」。

normal.en: Lover names a person, while love names the feeling or the person addressed, so the two words split the roles.
normal.cn: lover 指人，love 指感情或对对方的称呼，两个词分担了不同角色。

abstract.en: A suffix that turns a feeling into a person shows how English builds identities out of emotions.
abstract.cn: 一个把感情变成人的后缀，说明英语会用情感来构造身份。

abstract.en: The same word can name a concert fan and a secret partner, because both are defined by what they love.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指音乐会的粉丝，也能指秘密情人，因为两者都由「爱什么」来定义。

abstract.en: Lover reminds us that love is not only felt inside but always points at someone or something outside.
abstract.cn: lover 提醒人：爱不只是在心里感受，它总是指向外的某个人或某样东西。

definition_zh: 低的；矮的；低落的；低声的；低点；低水平
definition_en: not high or tall; below the usual level, amount or value; also sad, quiet or deep in sound, and a lowest point
core_image: 一只手掌压向地面，把一根横杆缓缓降到几乎贴着泥土的位置
scene: 傍晚的球场边，一个孩子把球贴着草地滚出去，球一路几乎不离开泥土。The ball stayed low and skimmed over the wet grass.
sceneCN: 这里 low 是「低的、贴近地面的」（第 1 个义项：高度低）；句意为球一直贴着地面，从湿草上滑过去。画面里可认出球场边、草地与滚动的球。

pos.zh: 低的；矮的；低落的；低声的

derivatives.zh: low 的比较级形式兼作动词，义为「降低；放下」
由 low 加形容词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「卑微的；地位低的」
由前缀 be- 与 low 构成，义为「在……下面；低于」
由 low 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「低；低落」

senses.title: Not high in height or position
senses.definition: having a small distance from the top to the ground, or standing near the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从顶部到地面的距离小，或位置接近地面的
senses.example: The shelf is low enough for a child to reach.
senses.exampleCN: 这个架子很低，孩子够得着。
senses.why: The oldest use describes a body or object near the ground, so lowness begins as a physical distance rather than a value.
senses.whyCN: 最早的用法描述人或物贴近地面的位置，所以「低」首先是一种空间距离，而不是价值判断。

senses.title: Below the usual level or amount
senses.definition: less than the normal, expected or average amount, level or value
senses.definitionCN: 低于正常、预期或平均的数量、水平或数值
senses.example: The river is unusually low this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 今年夏天这条河的水位异常低。
senses.why: Once the word can measure height, it can measure any scale, so a low river or a low price simply sits far down its own scale.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词能度量高度，就能度量任何尺度，于是低水位、低价格只是在自己的尺度上位置很靠下。

senses.title: Sad, weak or without energy
senses.definition: feeling unhappy, tired or without hope and energy
senses.definitionCN: 感到不快、疲惫，或缺少希望与精力
senses.example: He felt low for weeks after moving to the new city.
senses.exampleCN: 搬到新城市后，他情绪低落了几个星期。
senses.why: A low position is close to the ground, and English links that downward picture with a lowered spirit, so the word moves from space to mood.
senses.whyCN: 低的位置贴近地面，英语把这幅向下的画面与低落的精神联系起来，于是词义从空间转到情绪。

senses.title: Soft in volume or deep in pitch
senses.definition: produced quietly, or having a deep pitch rather than a high one
senses.definitionCN: 以较小的音量发出，或音调低沉而不高尖的
senses.example: She answered in a low voice so the others would not hear.
senses.exampleCN: 她低声回答，免得别人听见。
senses.why: A deep note sits at the bottom of the scale and a quiet voice carries less force, so both are heard as a kind of downward position.
senses.whyCN: 低沉的音处在音阶底部，轻声说话的力量也更小，两者听起来都像一种向下的位置。

senses.title: A low point, level or area
senses.definition: a point or level that is the lowest reached, or an area of low pressure in weather
senses.definitionCN: 所达到的最低点或最低水平，也指天气图上气压较低的区域
senses.example: Sales reached a new low in the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季销售额跌到了新的低点。
senses.why: Because the adjective can measure any scale, English turns it into a noun for the bottom value itself, and weather writers use it for low pressure.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词能度量各种尺度，英语就把它变成名词，指最低的那个数值本身，气象作者又用它指低气压。

intro.en: Low is an Old English adjective for being near the ground; it later spread from height to amounts, mood and sound.
intro.cn: low 是古英语中表示贴近地面的形容词，后来从高度扩展到数量、情绪与声音。

items.en: The adjective lāh meant low or humble, and it could describe both the ground and a person's rank.
items.cn: 形容词 lāh 意为低的、卑微的，既能形容地面，也能形容人的地位。

items.en: The reconstructed form is lauha-, rebuilt from related Germanic words such as Dutch laag.
items.cn: 其重构形式为 lauha-，是通过荷兰语 laag 等相关日耳曼词重建出来的。

items.en: Middle English lowe kept the physical sense and began to describe prices, voices and spirits.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lowe 保留物理义，并开始形容价格、嗓音与情绪。

items.en: Writers extended the word to any scale that could be measured, from income to temperature.
items.cn: 作家把这个词扩展到任何可度量的尺度，从收入到温度。

items.en: Modern English uses low for height, level, mood and voice, and as a noun for the lowest point.
items.cn: 现代英语用 low 指高度、水平、情绪与嗓音，也用作名词指最低点。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the low family and a spelling neighbour; the near-meaning group collects words for small height, small depth and low rank.
note.cn: 形近组收 low 词族与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示高度小、深度小与地位低的词。

entries.definition: The comparative of low, also a verb meaning to bring down.
entries.definitionCN: low 的比较级，也可作动词表示降低。

entries.definition: Humble in rank or position; built from low with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或身份卑微的；由 low 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Under or lower than something, built with be- and low.
entries.definitionCN: 在……下面或低于某物，由 be- 与 low 构成。

entries.definition: Not fast; only the spelling and rhyme are close, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢的；只是拼写与读音和 low 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having little height when said of a person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容人或物时表示个子矮、高度小。

entries.definition: Not deep, with little distance from top to bottom.
entries.definitionCN: 不深的，从顶到底距离很小。

entries.definition: Low in rank or importance, without pride.
entries.definitionCN: 地位或重要性低，不骄傲。

entries.definition: Making little or no sound.
entries.definitionCN: 发出很少声音或没有声音的。

entries.definition: Going far down from the top or surface.
entries.definitionCN: 从顶部或表面向下延伸很深的。

normalIntro.en: The word has been about being near the ground since Old English, and its family keeps returning to downward position, lower value and lowered feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 自古英语起这个词就表示贴近地面，同族词反复回到向下的位置、更低的值与低落的情绪。

normal.en: Old English lāh already meant low, so the word has kept its shape and sense for a very long time.
normal.cn: 古英语 lāh 已经表示低，所以这个词的形态与含义都保持了很长时间。

normal.en: The comparative is lower and the superlative is lowest, both made with the regular endings.
normal.cn: 比较级是 lower，最高级是 lowest，都用规则词尾构成。

normal.en: Below is be- plus low, literally at a lower place than something.
normal.cn: below 是 be- 加 low，字面就是「处于比某物更低的位置」。

normal.en: Low season names the quiet months of a trade, when prices and crowds are at their lowest.
normal.cn: low season 指行业的淡季，此时价格与客流都处在最低。

normal.en: Low point is a fixed phrase for the worst or weakest moment of a period.
normal.cn: low point 是固定说法，指一段时期里最糟或最弱的时刻。

abstract.en: A word that starts as a measurement of height ends up measuring mood, price and sound, because English reads downward as less.
abstract.cn: 一个从高度测量开始的词，最后用来测量情绪、价格与声音，因为英语把「向下」读作「更少」。

definition_zh: 运气；好运；侥幸；时运
definition_en: the force that seems to decide events by chance; also good fortune and success that comes without skill
core_image: 一枚硬币在空中翻转，落下时正好卡在指尖上方，摇摇欲坠却没有倒
scene: 码头边，渔夫把最后一网兜拉上来，网里空空的，可转身时却在木板上看见一枚别人掉下的硬币。Luck came to him at the very moment he had stopped expecting anything.
sceneCN: 这里 luck 是「好运、幸运」（第 2 个义项：带来好结果的好运）；句意为运气在他不再期待的时候降临。画面里可认出码头、空网兜与木板上的硬币。

senses.title: Chance seen as a force that shapes events
senses.definition: the force that seems to decide events by chance, whether the outcome is good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 似乎在冥冥中决定事情成败的偶然力量，无论结果是好是坏
senses.example: No one can explain why the storm missed the village; they put it down to luck.
senses.exampleCN: 谁也说不清风暴为什么绕过了村子，他们把它归因于运气。
senses.why: When people cannot explain why a plan succeeds or fails, they name the unknown cause luck, so the word first stands in for chance itself.
senses.whyCN: 当人们说不清一个计划为何成功或失败时，就把这个未知的原因叫作 luck，所以这个词最初是「偶然本身」的代称。

senses.title: Good fortune that brings favourable results
senses.definition: good fortune, especially when it brings success, safety or an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 尤指带来成功、平安或优势的好运气
senses.example: It was pure luck that the last seat went to her.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那个座位落到她手里，纯属好运。
senses.why: Because people most often speak of luck when things turn out well, the neutral force narrowed into the favourable sense that dominates everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们通常在事情顺利时才提起 luck，这个中性的力量就收窄成日常最常用的「好运气」义。

senses.title: Success that comes by chance rather than skill
senses.definition: a favourable result that happened by accident rather than through skill or planning
senses.definitionCN: 凭偶然而非技巧或计划取得的有利结果
senses.example: The team won by luck rather than by better play.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍是靠侥幸而不是靠更好的发挥赢的。
senses.why: If good fortune can deliver a result, then a result delivered that way is itself called luck, so the cause and the outcome share one word.
senses.whyCN: 如果好运能带来结果，那么以这种方式得到的结果本身也被叫作 luck，于是原因与结果共用同一个词。

senses.title: One's personal fortune at a particular time
senses.definition: the state of a person's fortune at a given moment, which can rise or fall
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在某一时刻的运气状态，可升可降
senses.example: His luck changed the moment the manager noticed his work.
senses.exampleCN: 经理注意到他的工作那一刻，他的运势就变了。
senses.why: Luck as a force can also be treated as something a person possesses, so English speaks of someone's luck rising, falling or running out.
senses.whyCN: 作为力量的 luck 也可以被看成一个人所拥有的东西，于是英语会说某人的运气上升、下降或用完。

intro.en: Luck enters English in the fifteenth century from a Germanic source; its exact path is uncertain, but gambling gave it a firm place in everyday speech.
intro.cn: luck 于十五世纪从日耳曼语来源进入英语；确切路径不确定，但赌博让它在日常语言中站稳了脚。

items.en: Luck appears in written English in the fifteenth century as lucke, meaning good fortune.
items.cn: luck 在十五世纪以 lucke 的形式出现在书面英语中，意为好运。

items.en: Most accounts link it to Middle Dutch luc or the related Low German gelucke, though the exact path is not certain.
items.cn: 多数说法把它与中古荷兰语 luc 或相关的低地德语 gelucke 联系起来，但确切来源路径并不确定。

items.en: In the sixteenth century the word was common at dice and card tables, where fortune was visibly decided by chance.
items.cn: 十六世纪时这个词常用于骰子和牌桌，在那里运气明显由偶然决定。

items.en: From games it widened to any event that people believed chance had decided.
items.cn: 它从游戏扩展到人们认为由偶然决定的任何事情。

items.en: Modern English uses luck for chance as a force, for good fortune, and for success that came without skill.
items.cn: 现代英语用 luck 指作为力量的偶然、好运气，以及不靠技巧而得来的成功。

abstract.en: A word for an unexplained cause becomes a word for a personal possession, because people would rather own fortune than admit they cannot explain it.

abstract.en: Luck sits between chance and fate: less planned than fate, more personal than pure chance.

abstract.en: Every wish of good luck admits the same thing: the outcome is not fully in our hands.

items.exampleCN: 她碰巧找到了那封信。

definition_zh: 幸运地；侥幸地；幸好；好在
definition_en: by good chance; fortunately, especially because something bad was avoided
core_image: 躲过一劫后长出一口气：刚才差一点就出事
scene: 差一步就要踩到积水的台阶，好在突然停住了脚步。I had already stepped out, but luckily there was a rail to catch.
sceneCN: 说话人差一点摔倒，最后抓住栏杆躲过一劫——这里 luckily 表示「幸好、侥幸躲过」（第 1 个义项：事情的结果偏向幸运一面）。

pos.zh: 幸运地；幸好（修饰整个句子）

senses.title: Happening by good fortune
senses.definition: used to say that something good happened because of chance, not because anyone planned it
senses.definitionCN: 指某件好事因偶然机会发生，并非事先安排所致
senses.example: Luckily, the train was delayed, so we did not miss it.
senses.exampleCN: 幸好火车晚点了，我们才没错过。
senses.why: The adverb grows straight out of the noun luck: when luck works in your favor, the whole outcome turns out well.
senses.whyCN: 副词直接从名词 luck 长出来：运气站在你这一边，整个结果就朝好的方向发展。

senses.title: Escaping a bad result narrowly
senses.definition: used when something bad almost happened but was avoided by chance
senses.definitionCN: 指坏事几乎发生，却因偶然因素得以避免
senses.example: He fell off the ladder but luckily landed on a pile of leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 他从梯子上摔下来，但侥幸落在一堆树叶上。
senses.why: The core image is the near miss: luck intervenes at the last moment so the danger stays unreal.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「差一点出事」：运气在最后一刻介入，危险始终没有成真。

senses.title: Adding a grateful comment to a statement
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to show relief that a situation was not worse
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，表示庆幸情况没有更糟
senses.example: Luckily for us, the shop still had one ticket left.
senses.exampleCN: 对我们来说幸运的是，商店还剩一张票。
senses.why: English often turns adverbs into sentence-level comments; luckily works like fortunately to color the whole clause.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把副词用作整句的评注；luckily 和 fortunately 一样为整个句子染上庆幸的语气。

intro.en: Luckily is a young English adverb built directly on the noun luck, a word with northern Germanic roots.
intro.cn: luckily 是一个较年轻的英语副词，直接建立在名词 luck 之上，而 luck 源自北部日耳曼语。

items.en: The noun luck is generally traced to Old Norse happ, later a personal name Lukka, meaning chance or good fortune.
items.cn: 名词 luck 一般追溯到古诺斯语 happ（后作人名 Lukka），意为机会或好运。

items.en: Northern Dutch and Low German kept related forms such as luk, which helped carry the word into northern English speech.
items.cn: 荷兰北部与低地德语保留了 luk 等相关形式，帮助该词进入英格兰北部口语。

items.en: In Middle English luck meant fortune or chance, especially good fortune, and spread from the north to the whole country.
items.cn: 中古英语中 luck 意为运气或机会，尤指好运，并从北方扩散到全国。

items.en: The wider Germanic family links luck with words for happiness, since happ is also the source of happy.
items.cn: 更广的日耳曼语族把 luck 与「幸福」类词汇联系起来，因为 happ 同时也是 happy 的来源。

items.en: The adverb luckily formed in Modern English as luck plus the adverbial suffix -ly, first recorded in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 现代英语中 luckily 由 luck 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，最早见于十六世纪。

note.en: These neighbors either share luck as a base or compete with luckily in meaning.
note.cn: 这些邻近词要么共享词根 luck，要么在意义上与 luckily 相互竞争。

entries.definitionCN: 可指侥幸，也可指快乐地，语义更宽

entries.definitionCN: 习语：碰巧（可指好运也可指坏运）

normalIntro.en: Five ways to anchor luckily through its family and grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 从词族和语法两个角度记住 luckily 的五条线索。

normal.en: luck + -ly: turn the noun luck into an adverb.
normal.cn: luck 加副词后缀 -ly：把名词「运气」变成副词。

normal.en: lucky is the adjective pair; luckily is its adverb twin.
normal.cn: lucky 是形容词搭档，luckily 是它的副词孪生兄弟。

normal.en: Sentence adverb: luckily can stand at the front with a comma.
normal.cn: 作句首副词：luckily 可放在句首并用逗号隔开。

normal.en: Compare happily: luck and happ both mean good chance.
normal.cn: 对照 happily：luck 与 happ（幸福）本是同源意象。

normal.en: Frequently tells how often; luckily tells how the dice fell.
normal.cn: frequently 说频率，luckily 说骰子掷出的结果。

abstract.en: Picture a coin landing heads at the exact second you needed it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币恰好在最需要的时刻正面朝上落地。

abstract.en: See a falling plate caught just before it hits the floor.
abstract.cn: 看见一个盘子坠向地面、在摔碎前一秒被接住。

abstract.en: Feel the relief in one long breath after the danger passes.
abstract.cn: 危险过后长长舒一口气的庆幸感。

examples.en: Luckily, the fire alarm rang before the smoke spread.
examples.cn: 幸好火警在烟雾蔓延前就响了。

examples.en: She had no umbrella, but luckily a stranger offered to share his.
examples.cn: 她没带伞，但幸好一位陌生人愿意与他共用。

examples.en: He guessed the last answer, and it turned out to be right.
examples.cn: 他猜了最后一道题的答案，结果竟然对了。

sensesIntro.en: From plain good luck to narrow escapes and a grateful sentence comment.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单纯的好运，到惊险脱险，再到句首庆幸的语气词。

branches.cn: 说话人把庆幸作为对整句的评注。

branches.cn: 惊险脱险自然引出庆幸之情。

definition_zh: 幸运的；走运的；带来好运的；吉利的；侥幸的
definition_en: having good fortune; bringing good fortune; happening by chance in a favourable way; or believed to be auspicious
core_image: 一个人从口袋里摸出一张旧彩票，对着光一看，号码正好全部对上
scene: 雨刚停，一个赶路的人随手招了一下，空荡荡的街口竟真的停下一辆出租车。He felt lucky as the taxi pulled up beside him.
sceneCN: 这里 lucky 是「幸运的、走运的」（第 1 个义项：本人有好运）；句意为出租车在他身边停下时，他感到自己很走运。画面里可认出雨后的街口与停下的出租车。

pos.zh: 幸运的；走运的；带来好运的；吉利的；侥幸的

collocations.zh: 难得的好机会；意外的好运

senses.title: Having good fortune in a particular situation
senses.definition: enjoying good fortune, especially when something good happens by chance
senses.definitionCN: 享有好运，尤指好事偶然落到自己头上
senses.example: She felt lucky when the last ticket was still available.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一张票还没卖掉，她觉得自己很幸运。
senses.why: The noun luck names the force, and the suffix -y turns it into a quality, so a person can be described as having that force on their side.
senses.whyCN: 名词 luck 指这种力量，后缀 -y 把它变成一种性质，于是可以说一个人身上带着这种力量。

senses.title: Believed to bring good fortune to its owner
senses.definition: thought to bring good fortune to the person who has it or carries it
senses.definitionCN: 被认为能给拥有者或携带者带来好运的
senses.example: He wore the same shirt to every match because he believed it was lucky.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢比赛他都穿同一件衬衫，因为他相信那件衣服能带来好运。
senses.why: If a person can be lucky, then an object can be trusted to carry that luck, so the word spreads from people to charms and clothes.
senses.whyCN: 既然人可以走运，人们也会相信某件物品能承载这份运气，于是词义从人扩展到护身符和衣物。

senses.title: Happening by chance in a favourable way
senses.definition: favourable but produced by accident rather than by skill or knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 结果有利，却出自偶然而非技巧或知识
senses.example: It was a lucky guess, not real knowledge.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是侥幸猜中，并不是真懂。
senses.why: When a good result arrives without skill, English calls it lucky, because the outcome is credited to fortune rather than to the person.
senses.whyCN: 当好结果并非来自技巧时，英语称其为 lucky，因为这个结果被归功于运气而不是归功于人。

senses.title: Considered auspicious for a particular purpose
senses.definition: believed to be a favourable time, number or sign for something
senses.definitionCN: 被认为对某件事有利的时间、数字或征兆
senses.example: They chose the date because it was a lucky day in the old calendar.
senses.exampleCN: 他们选这个日期，是因为它在旧历里是幸运日。
senses.why: From charms the word extends to days, numbers and signs, because people look for fortune not only in objects but also in timing.
senses.whyCN: 从护身符出发，这个词又扩展到日子、数字与征兆，因为人们不只在物件里找运气，也在时机里找。

intro.en: Lucky is the noun luck with the adjective suffix -y; the noun itself came into English from a Germanic source whose exact path is uncertain.
intro.cn: lucky 是名词 luck 加形容词后缀 -y；这个名词本身来自日耳曼语来源，确切路径不确定。

items.en: Luck enters English in the fifteenth century, and the adjective lucky follows by adding -y to the noun.
items.cn: luck 于十五世纪进入英语，形容词 lucky 由名词加 -y 随后产生。

items.en: The noun is generally linked to Middle Dutch luc or Low German gelucke, though the exact source remains uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词一般认为与中古荷兰语 luc 或低地德语 gelucke 有关，确切来源仍不确定。

items.en: Lucky appears in the sixteenth century, first around games of chance and then in ordinary speech.
items.cn: lucky 在十六世纪出现，最初用于碰运气的游戏，后来进入日常语言。

items.en: The suffix -y turns nouns into adjectives, as it does in health to healthy and luck to lucky.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 把名词变成形容词，health 变 healthy、luck 变 lucky 都是这样。

items.en: Modern English uses lucky for people, charms, guesses, breaks and auspicious days.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lucky 形容人、护身符、猜测、好机会与吉日。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the luck family and a word that merely rhymes; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for good fortune and its opposite.
note.cn: 形近组收 luck 词族与一个只是押韵的词；近义组收表示好运及其反面的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun behind lucky, meaning chance or good fortune.
entries.definitionCN: lucky 背后的名词，意为运气或好运。

entries.definition: By good fortune; the adverb built from lucky.
entries.definitionCN: 幸运地；由 lucky 构成的副词。

entries.definition: Having bad fortune; lucky with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 运气不好的；lucky 加否定前缀 un-。

entries.definition: Brave in a difficult situation; only the ending is close, and the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 在困境中勇敢的；只是词尾与 lucky 相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: Having good fortune, often in a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 有好运的，语气常较正式。

entries.definition: Enjoying good fortune that is seen as a gift.
entries.definitionCN: 享有被视为恩赐的好运。

entries.definition: Given special help, advantage or preference.
entries.definitionCN: 得到特别帮助、优势或偏爱的。

entries.definition: Protected as if by magic; often a light or ironic word.
entries.definitionCN: 像受魔法保护般的；常带轻松或反讽语气。

entries.definition: Marked by bad fortune from the start.
entries.definitionCN: 从一开始就注定倒霉的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent suffix build from luck, so its hooks come from the noun, the -y suffix and the spelling changes in comparison.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由 luck 加后缀清楚构成，记忆钩子来自名词、-y 后缀以及比较级中的拼写变化。

normal.en: Lucky is luck plus -y, so the adjective means having or carrying luck.
normal.cn: lucky 是 luck 加 -y，所以这个形容词意为拥有或带着运气。

normal.en: The comparative is luckier: the final y becomes i before -er is added.
normal.cn: 比较级是 luckier：最后的 y 先变成 i，再加 -er。

normal.en: The superlative is luckiest, following the same y to i change.
normal.cn: 最高级是 luckiest，同样先把 y 变成 i。

normal.en: Unlucky adds the prefix un- to lucky and reverses the fortune.
normal.cn: unlucky 在 lucky 前加前缀 un-，把运气反过来。

normal.en: Lucky break and lucky charm are fixed phrases, one for a chance opportunity and one for a trusted object.
normal.cn: lucky break 与 lucky charm 是固定短语，一个指偶然得来的机会，一个指被信赖的物件。

abstract.en: Calling a shirt lucky shows how easily people move fortune out of the body and into an object they can control.
abstract.cn: 把一件衬衫说成幸运，说明人很容易把运气从身体转移到一件自己能控制的物品上。

abstract.en: A lucky guess is praised and distrusted at once, because we want the result but not the randomness behind it.
abstract.cn: 侥幸猜中同时得到赞许与怀疑，因为我们想要结果，却不喜欢结果背后的偶然。

abstract.en: A lucky day is a way of making time itself take sides with a plan.
abstract.cn: 吉日是一种让时间本身站在计划一边的说法。

examples.en: She felt lucky when the last ticket was still available.
examples.cn: 最后一张票还没卖掉，她觉得自己很幸运。

examples.en: He wore the same shirt to every match because he believed it was lucky.
examples.cn: 每逢比赛他都穿同一件衬衫，因为他相信那件衣服能带来好运。

examples.en: It was a lucky guess, not real knowledge.
examples.cn: 那只是侥幸猜中，并不是真懂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉齐」——队伍拉得齐，运气自然来，记住 lucky 是幸运的。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is having good fortune; the senses spread to objects that carry luck, results that come by accident and times believed to be auspicious.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是本人拥有好运；义项扩展到承载运气的物件、偶然得来的结果，以及被认为吉利的时机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulling an old ticket from a pocket and finding every number matches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从口袋里摸出一张旧彩票，发现号码全部对上。

branches.en: a traveller who finds the last taxi in the rain
branches.cn: 雨中赶上最后一辆出租车的行人

branches.en: a shirt worn again for every important match
branches.cn: 每场重要比赛都重穿的那件衬衫

branches.en: a small charm kept in a coat pocket
branches.cn: 放在外套口袋里的护身符

branches.en: a date chosen because the old calendar favours it

intro.cn: lucky 是名词 luck 加 -y 构成，它的词族又加上比较级、否定前缀与名词后缀。

items.exampleCN: 运气帮他们重新找到了路。

items.example: They were lucky to escape the storm.
items.exampleCN: 他们躲过风暴，真是幸运。

items.example: This year has been luckier than the last.
items.exampleCN: 这一年比去年更幸运。

items.example: That was the luckiest day of his life.
items.exampleCN: 那是他一生中最幸运的一天。

items.example: Luckily, nobody was hurt.
items.exampleCN: 幸好没有人受伤。

items.example: Some actors think the play is unlucky.
items.exampleCN: 有些演员认为这部剧不吉利。

items.example: Luckiness adds -ness to lucky.

senses.title: A solid mass with no regular shape
senses.definition: a piece of solid material that has no regular shape and is felt as one heavy mass
senses.definitionCN: 一块没有规则形状、被感知为一整个沉重整体的固体
senses.example: He dropped a lump of sugar into the hot tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他往热茶里丢了一块方糖。
senses.why: The word starts from what the hand feels: a portion of material that has set or been pressed into one body, with no edges worth counting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从手的触感出发：一部分材料凝成或压成了一整块，边上没有值得去数的棱角。

senses.title: A swelling under the skin
senses.definition: an area of the body that has risen into a hard or rounded swelling
senses.definitionCN: 身体上隆起的一块硬或圆形的肿大部位
senses.example: She found a small lump on her arm and had it checked.
senses.exampleCN: 她发现手臂上有个小肿块，就去做了检查。
senses.why: A swelling has the same outline as a mass of clay or coal, so the body borrows the word for anything that pushes up under the skin.
senses.whyCN: 肿块与一团黏土或煤块的轮廓相同，于是身体借用了这个词，指任何在皮下顶起来的东西。

senses.title: To group things into one mass
senses.definition: to put separate people or things into one group without sorting them
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的人或物不加区分地放进同一组
senses.example: The report lumps all the small shops together as one category.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把所有小店归并成同一类。
senses.why: If separate pieces are thrown into one pile, their edges disappear into a single mass; the verb is that throwing, applied to facts and categories.
senses.whyCN: 如果把分开的块丢进同一堆，它们的边就消失在一整团里；动词就是这一「丢」，只是对象换成了事实与类别。

senses.title: To accept something unpleasant
senses.definition: to swallow an unpleasant situation because it cannot be changed
senses.definitionCN: 因为无法改变而把不愉快的处境硬吞下去
senses.example: He did not like the decision, but he had to lump it.
senses.exampleCN: 他不喜欢这个决定，但也只能忍着接受。
senses.why: The phrase like it or lump it pictures the bad news as one hard lump that must be swallowed whole, since there is no way to chew it into smaller pieces.
senses.whyCN: like it or lump it 把坏消息想成一整块硬东西：既然没法嚼碎，就只能整块吞下。

intro.en: Lump is a Middle English noun for a shapeless mass; its deeper origin is uncertain, and the verb and medical senses grew from that solid block.
intro.cn: lump 是中古英语中表示「无定形一块」的名词；它更早的来源不确定，动词义与医学义都是从这块固体生长出来的。

items.en: The noun lump, also written lompe, first names a shapeless mass of material, neither shaped nor measured.
items.cn: 名词 lump 也写作 lompe，最初指一块既无形状也无定量的材料。

items.en: A common suggestion compares Middle Dutch lomp, a rag or a clumsy piece, and German Lumpen, a rag; the comparison is offered as possible, not as settled.
items.cn: 一种常见说法把它与中古荷兰语 lomp（破布、笨重的一块）和德语 Lumpen（破布）相比较；这只是一条可能的线索，并非定论。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense of throwing separate things into one mass, which gives phrases such as lump together and later lump sum.
items.cn: 动词义出现，意思是把分开的东西丢成一整堆，由此产生 lump together 以及后来的 lump sum 等说法。

items.en: Medical writers use lump for a swelling felt under the skin, and the same outline produces the phrase a lump in the throat for strong emotion.
items.cn: 医学作者用 lump 指皮下摸到的肿块；同样的轮廓又产生 a lump in the throat 这一说法，用来形容情绪激动。

items.en: Phrases such as take one's lumps and like it or lump it keep the sense of a hard thing that simply has to be borne.
items.cn: take one's lumps 与 like it or lump it 之类的说法，保留了「一块硬东西只能硬扛」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and derivatives built on lump; the near-meaning group gathers words for masses, pieces and swellings.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lump 构成的变形与派生词；近义组收表示块状物、团块与肿起的词。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the name of a shapeless mass, and its family keeps returning to hard pieces, swellings and things thrown into one pile.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一团无定形材料的名字，同族词反复回到硬块、肿起以及被丢成一堆的东西。

normal.en: Lump is first a noun for a shapeless mass; the verb comes later and means to throw separate things into one pile.
normal.cn: lump 首先是名词，指无定形的一团；动词义较晚出现，意思是把分开的东西丢成一堆。

normal.en: Lump together keeps that picture: separate pieces lose their edges once they are dropped into the same heap.
normal.cn: lump together 保留了这个画面：分开的块一旦被丢进同一堆，就失去了各自的边。

normal.en: A lump of sugar is a small pressed block, which shows how loose the word is about exact shape.
normal.cn: 一块方糖就是压成的小方块，可见这个词对具体形状并不严格。

normal.en: A lump on the arm is a swelling shaped like a mass under the skin, so the medical sense borrows the physical one.
normal.cn: 手臂上的肿块就是皮下形似一团的东西，医学义直接借用了物理义。

normal.en: Like it or lump it means swallow the bad news whole, as if it were one hard lump with no way to chew it.
normal.cn: like it or lump it 意为把坏消息整块吞下，好像那是一块没法嚼的硬东西。

abstract.en: A lump has no edges to hold, which is why the word suits anything we cannot easily take apart.
abstract.cn: 一块 lump 没有可抓的棱角，所以这个词适合形容任何我们难以拆开的东西。

abstract.en: To lump people together is to lose the outlines that made them separate, and that is exactly the harm the verb describes.
abstract.cn: 把人 lump together，就是丢掉让他们彼此分开的轮廓，而这正是这个动词所指的害处。

abstract.en: A hard lump can be swallowed but not digested, which is a fair picture of a truth we accept without liking.
abstract.cn: 硬块吞得下却消化不了，这正好形容我们接受却并不喜欢的真相。

senses.title: A device that performs work
senses.definition: an assembly of connected parts that uses power to carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 由相连部件构成、使用动力完成任务的组合体
senses.example: The machine lifts the load with a single lever.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器只用一个手柄就抬起货物。
senses.why: the Greek noun named any contrivance, so the first sense is the broad one of a built device.
senses.whyCN: 希腊名词原指任何巧妙装置，因此第一个义项就是「人造装置」这一宽泛含义。

senses.title: A computer
senses.definition: the computing hardware that executes stored instructions
senses.definitionCN: 执行已存指令的计算硬件
senses.example: The machine rebooted before the backup finished.
senses.exampleCN: 备份还没完成，机器就重启了。
senses.why: computers became the most common machine in daily life, and speakers shortened the name.
senses.whyCN: 计算机成了日常最常见的机器，说话者就把名称缩短了。

senses.title: A household or workshop appliance
senses.definition: a named device for one task, as in a washing or sewing machine
senses.definitionCN: 为单一任务命名的装置，如洗衣机或缝纫机
senses.example: The sewing machine has outlived three owners.
senses.exampleCN: 那台缝纫机已经比三位主人活得都久。
senses.why: a device is named by its task plus this general word, which is how the compound names spread.
senses.whyCN: 装置以「任务＋这个总称」命名，这类复合名称就是这样扩散的。

senses.title: A machine tool

senses.example: The new machine holds a tolerance of a hundredth of a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 这台新机床能保持百分之一毫米的公差。
senses.why: in a workshop, the general word often means the tool that makes other parts.
senses.whyCN: 在车间里，这个总称常指制造其他零件的工具。

senses.title: To cut or shape by machine
senses.definition: to remove material or form a part with a powered tool

senses.exampleCN: 他们分两道工序加工了那块坯料。

senses.whyCN: 当工具的动作需要一个名称时，名词就变成了动词。

senses.title: A political organisation
senses.definition: the permanent staff and structure that win elections or hold power
senses.definitionCN: 赢得选举或维持权力的常设人员与结构
senses.example: The party machine decided the candidate before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 政党机器在投票之前就决定了候选人。
senses.why: an organisation that runs without sentiment is described by the most impersonal noun available.
senses.whyCN: 不带感情运转的组织，就用最非人格的名词来描述。

senses.title: An impersonal system of rule
senses.definition: the administrative apparatus of a state or large institution
senses.definitionCN: 国家或大型机构的行政装置
senses.example: The state machine ground down every small request.
senses.exampleCN: 国家机器把每一个小请求都磨掉了。
senses.why: the image of interlocking parts describes bureaucracy better than any abstract word.
senses.whyCN: 「咬合的部件」这一意象，比任何抽象词都更能描述官僚体系。

senses.title: A person who acts automatically
senses.definition: a person treated as incapable of independent thought
senses.definitionCN: 被视为无法独立思考的人
senses.example: They turned him into a machine that answered tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把他变成一台只回答工单的机器。
senses.why: calling a person a machine denies judgement, which is the insult the word carries here.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作机器就是否认其判断力，这正是这个词在此处的贬义。

senses.title: Automated by computation
senses.definition: used before a noun for processes carried out by computers
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指由计算机完成的过程
senses.example: Machine translation improved, but it still misses tone.
senses.exampleCN: 机器翻译进步了，却仍抓不住语气。
senses.why: as a modifier, the word marks the shift from human to computed action.
senses.whyCN: 作修饰语时，这个词标记从人工到计算动作的转移。

senses.title: The power unit of a vehicle
senses.definition: the engine and its housing in a boat, train or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 船、火车或车辆中的发动机及其外壳
senses.example: The fire machine kept its pump running for nine hours.
senses.exampleCN: 消防车的泵持续运转了九个小时。
senses.why: early industrial English called a powered vehicle a machine, and the usage survives in a few names.
senses.whyCN: 早期工业英语把动力车辆叫作 machine，这种用法在少数名称里留存下来。

intro.en: Machine came from Greek mekhane through Latin machina and French. It meant any contrivance long before it meant a powered device, and its computing and organisational senses are later extensions.
intro.cn: machine 经拉丁语 machina 与法语来自希腊语 mekhane。它很久以前指任何巧妙装置，之后才指动力装置；计算机义与组织义是更晚的延伸。

items.en: Greek mekhane named a device, especially a stage crane or a siege engine, and also a means or expedient.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置，尤指舞台吊机或攻城器械，也指手段与办法。

items.en: Latin machina meant a structure, scaffold or engine, and the phrase deus ex machina came from the stage crane.
items.cn: 拉丁语 machina 指结构、脚手架或器械，短语 deus ex machina 就来自舞台吊机。

items.en: French machine entered English in the seventeenth century and covered any constructed device, not only powered ones.
items.cn: 法语 machine 在十七世纪进入英语，指任何建造出来的装置，而不只是动力装置。

items.en: Steam and factory work narrowed machine toward devices with moving parts driven by power.
items.cn: 蒸汽与工厂作业把 machine 收窄为由动力驱动、带运动部件的装置。

items.en: The twentieth century added the computer and the party machine, both built on the image of parts working together.
items.cn: 二十世纪加上计算机与政党机器两义，二者都建立在「部件协同运转」的意象上。

items.en: Machining arose in workshops as the verb for what a machine tool does to metal.
items.cn: machining 在车间里产生，指机床对金属所做的加工。

note.en: The first group is the machine family in other shapes; the second group is the neighbouring words for devices and systems.
note.cn: 第一组是 machine 词族的其他形态；第二组是装置与体系的相邻说法。

entries.definition: Machines as a mass; one machine is countable, machinery is not.
entries.definitionCN: 指机器的整体；一台机器可数，machinery 不可数。

entries.definition: A person who operates or makes machines; the noun names the equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作或制造机器的人；名词指设备。

entries.definition: A person who repairs machines; a machine is the thing repaired.
entries.definitionCN: 指修理机器的人；machine 是被修的东西。

entries.definition: The set of parts that produces a motion; a machine contains one or more mechanisms.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生运动的那组部件；一台机器包含一个或多个机构。

entries.definition: Any constructed thing made for a purpose, often small; a machine usually has moving parts and power.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的造的任何东西，常指小型；machine 通常有运动部件与动力。

entries.definition: A machine that converts energy into motion; it is a part of many machines.
entries.definitionCN: 把能量转成运动的机器；它是许多机器的一个部件。

entries.definition: An implement a person holds and guides; a machine supplies its own motion.
entries.definitionCN: 由人握持与引导的器具；machine 自己提供运动。

entries.definition: A set of equipment working as one, often for an experiment or an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体工作的一整套设备，常用于实验或机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Greek source and the real noun-verb pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实希腊语来源与真实名词动词成对关系。

normal.en: Mekhane meant a stage crane, so a machine is first a thing that lifts and moves.
normal.cn: mekhane 原指舞台吊机，所以 machine 首先是能吊起与移动东西的装置。

normal.en: The verb forms are regular: machines, machined, machined, machining.
normal.cn: 动词形式规则：machines、machined、machined、machining。

normal.en: Task names build on it: washing machine, sewing machine, machine tool.
normal.cn: 任务名称在它之上构成：洗衣机、缝纫机、机床。

normal.en: The computing sense is simply the shortened name of the most common machine.
normal.cn: 计算机义不过是「最常用机器」的简称。

normal.en: Two objects split the verb: machine a part, machine a surface.
normal.cn: 两类宾语分开动词：加工一个零件，加工一个表面。

abstract.en: Picture a crane on a stage lowering a god who is only a painted board.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上的吊机放下一个神，而那神不过是一块画板。

abstract.en: Picture a lathe turning a shaft until the metal is exactly the size of an idea.
abstract.cn: 想象车床削一根轴，直到金属恰好等于一个想法的尺寸。

abstract.en: Picture an office where every request disappears into a slot and comes out stamped.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，每个请求都落进一个槽口，再盖着章出来。

examples.en: The machine does the lifting, but a person still chooses where.
examples.cn: 机器负责起吊，但选择吊到哪里仍由人决定。

examples.en: They machined the replacement part overnight.
examples.cn: 他们连夜加工了那只替换零件。

examples.en: The party machine had chosen the nominee months earlier.
examples.cn: 政党机器几个月前就已定下候选人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马（ma）身（chine）」——马拉着的一副身架，就是最早干活的机器

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置、舞台吊机」→ 拉丁 machina「结构、器械」→ 法语 machine → 英语 machine；先泛指装置，工业时代收窄为动力装置，二十世纪扩展出计算机与组织体系义，动词指机床加工。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses run from the general device to the computer, the appliance, the machine tool, the verb, the party machine, the state apparatus, the dehumanised person, computed processes and the vehicle's power unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从泛指的装置出发，经过计算机、家用器具、机床、动词用法、政党机器、国家机器、被机械化的人、计算化流程，最后到车辆动力机组。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lathe holding a metal shaft while a cutter advances and curls off chips.
core.cn: 核心意象：车床夹着一段金属轴，刀头推进，铁屑卷曲落下。

branches.en: DEVICES: any working assembly, and the named appliance built on that pattern.
branches.cn: 装置：任何做功的组合体，以及按此模式命名的器具。

branches.en: COMPUTATION: the computer itself, and processes carried out by computed action.
branches.cn: 计算：计算机本身，以及由计算动作完成的过程。

branches.en: TOOL AND ACTION: the machine tool, and the verb for what it does to metal.
branches.cn: 工具与动作：机床，以及它对金属所做加工的动词。

branches.en: ORGANISED POWER: the party machine, and the administrative apparatus of a state.
branches.cn: 组织化的权力：政党机器，以及国家的行政装置。

branches.en: THE MECHANICAL FIGURE: a person reduced to a machine, and a vehicle's engine unit.
branches.cn: 机械化的形象：被降为机器的人，以及车辆的动力机组。

intro.en: Machine is a borrowed noun with no living affix; its family adds -ery, -ist, -ing and compound forms.
intro.cn: machine 是借入名词，本身没有能产的词缀；其词族另加 -ery、-ist、-ing 与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin machina is the direct source of the French and English forms; the Greek noun mekhane stands behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 machina 是法语与英语形式的直接来源，其背后是希腊名词 mekhane。

items.example: The Greek noun carries both the machine and the trick.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词兼有「机器」与「计策」两面。

items.example: Latin widened the noun to any built structure.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个名词扩大到任何建造的结构。

items.meaning: device; to cut with a tool
items.example: English uses the same form for the object and the action.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一形式指对象与动作。

items.example: The ending produces the uncountable collective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾产生不可数的集合名词。

items.example: The ending names the operator.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指操作者。

items.example: The ending names the cutting work itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指切削工作本身。

items.example: The ending marks what a device can read or do.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记装置能读或能做的事。

items.example: The ending names one arrangement of moving parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指一套运动部件的组合。

senses.title: Machines as a collective body
senses.definition: a group of machines considered together, especially in a workplace
senses.definitionCN: 被一并看待的一组机器，尤指工作场所中的
senses.example: The plant bought new machinery before hiring new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂先买新机械，再招新员工。
senses.why: the -ery ending makes a mass noun, so the word names machines as a body rather than one machine.
senses.whyCN: -ery 词尾构成集合名词，因此这个词指一批机器，而不是一台机器。

senses.title: The working parts inside a machine
senses.definition: the internal parts that transmit motion in a device
senses.definitionCN: 在装置内部传递运动的部件
senses.example: The clock's machinery needed oil, not a new face.
senses.exampleCN: 这座钟的机械部件需要上油，而不是换表盘。
senses.why: the collective noun also covers the parts that make one machine work, since they too are a set.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词也指使单台机器运转的那组部件，因为它们同样成组。

senses.title: The apparatus of an organisation
senses.definition: the people, offices and procedures that keep an institution running
senses.definitionCN: 维持一个机构运转的人员、部门与程序
senses.example: Reform stalled inside the machinery of the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 改革在部委的机构内部停住了。
senses.why: an organisation works through parts that transmit decisions, exactly as gears transmit motion.
senses.whyCN: 组织靠传递决定的部件运作，正如齿轮传递运动。

senses.title: A process treated as a system
senses.titleCN: 被当作系统看待的流程
senses.definition: the arrangeable steps by which something is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 完成某事时可加以安排的那些步骤
senses.example: The machinery of appeal is slow but predictable.
senses.exampleCN: 申诉的运作机制缓慢，却可预期。
senses.why: once steps are regular enough to be described, they can be spoken of as machinery.
senses.whyCN: 当步骤规律到可以被描述，人们就会把它说成机械装置。

senses.title: Farm equipment as a class
senses.definition: the tractors and implements used in farming, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 农业中使用的拖拉机与农具的总和
senses.example: Shared machinery let small farms afford a harvester.
senses.exampleCN: 共用机械让小农场也买得起收割机。
senses.why: the collective noun is the natural way to speak of a category of equipment bought and kept together.
senses.whyCN: 集合名词是谈论「成套购买与保管」的设备类别的自然方式。

senses.title: Stage and studio equipment
senses.definition: the rigging and devices that move scenery or sets
senses.definitionCN: 移动布景或场地的吊装与装置
senses.example: The theatre's machinery was hidden behind the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 剧院的舞台机械藏在幕布之后。
senses.why: theatre has used hidden devices for centuries, and the collective word names them without exposure.
senses.whyCN: 剧院使用隐蔽装置已有数百年，集合名词正好不必把它们露出来。

senses.title: The mechanism of an abstract force
senses.definition: the system by which a large process such as war or law is conducted
senses.definitionCN: 战争或法律等大型过程得以进行的系统
senses.example: The machinery of war outlived the government that built it.
senses.exampleCN: 战争的机器比建立它的政府活得更久。
senses.why: the figurative use extends to anything vast, impersonal and hard to stop.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法延伸到一切庞大、非人格且难以停止的事物。

senses.title: Heavy equipment on a site
senses.definition: the excavators and cranes that do the heavy physical work
senses.definitionCN: 从事繁重体力作业的挖掘机与起重机
senses.example: Heavy machinery arrived before the surveyors finished.
senses.exampleCN: 重型机械在测量员完工之前就进场了。
senses.why: on a site, the word means the class of large powered equipment, not a single tool.
senses.whyCN: 在工地上，这个词指大型动力设备这一类别，而不是单件工具。

intro.en: Machinery is a collective noun built on machine, which comes from Greek mekhane through Latin machina and French. The -ery ending turns one device into a body of devices.
intro.cn: machinery 是在 machine 上构成的集合名词，而 machine 经拉丁语 machina 与法语来自希腊语 mekhane。-ery 词尾把一台装置变成一批装置。

items.en: Greek mekhane meant a device, an engine of war or a means of doing something.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置、攻城器械或做事的手段。

items.en: Latin machina named a structure, scaffold or engine, and kept the Greek sense of a contrivance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 machina 指结构、脚手架或器械，保留了希腊语「巧妙装置」的意思。

items.en: French machine carried the word into English in the seventeenth century, at first for any structure or device.
items.cn: 法语 machine 在十七世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指任何结构或装置。

items.en: English machine narrowed toward powered devices as steam and industry spread.
items.cn: 随着蒸汽与工业扩散，英语 machine 逐渐收窄为动力装置。

items.en: The ending -ery, from French -erie, gathers things into a mass or a trade, giving machinery, cutlery and stationery.
items.cn: 词尾 -ery 来自法语 -erie，把事物聚成整体或行业，形成 machinery、cutlery、stationery 这类词。

items.en: Bureaucracy and warfare gave the collective word its modern figurative sense of an impersonal working system.
items.cn: 官僚制度与战争给了这个集合词现代比喻义：非人格的运作系统。

note.en: The first group is the machine root in different shapes and counts; the second group is the neighbouring collective and system words.
note.cn: 第一组是「机器」词根的不同形态与单复数；第二组是相邻的集合与系统说法。

entries.definition: A single device; machinery is the mass of such devices, so it takes no plural.
entries.definitionCN: 指单台装置；machinery 是这类装置的整体，因此没有复数。

entries.definition: The person who runs a machine; the collective noun names the equipment, not the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 指操作机器的人；集合名词指设备，不指工人。

entries.definition: A particular arrangement of parts that produces motion; machinery is the wider set.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生运动的某套部件组合；machinery 是更大的集合。

entries.definition: Of machines or done without thought; the noun machinery carries only the equipment sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指机器的或不假思索的；名词 machinery 只保留设备义。

entries.definition: Any set of items needed for a purpose; machinery is specifically powered machines.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的所需的一整套物件；machinery 特指动力机器。

entries.definition: A set of parts working together for a function, often in science or politics.
entries.definitionCN: 为一功能共同运作的一整套部件，常用于科学或政治语境。

entries.definition: An organised set of parts or steps; machinery is the concrete or institutional version.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的部件或步骤集合；machinery 是其具体或建制化的版本。

entries.definition: The buildings and machines of an industrial site taken as one unit.
entries.definitionCN: 把一个工业场所的建筑与机器当作一个整体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real suffix and the real collective phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实词尾与真实集合搭配。

normal.en: The -ery ending makes a mass noun, as in cutlery and stationery.
normal.cn: -ery 词尾构成集合名词，如 cutlery、stationery。

normal.en: It takes no plural: one says much machinery, not many machineries.
normal.cn: 它没有复数：说 much machinery，而不说 many machineries。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: heavy machinery, agricultural machinery, industrial machinery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：重型机械、农业机械、工业机械。

normal.en: The figurative sense needs a system: the machinery of government, the machinery of justice.
normal.cn: 比喻义要接一个体系：政府机构、司法机制。

normal.en: One machine is a machine; a hall full of them is machinery.
normal.cn: 一台叫 a machine，一屋子就是 machinery。

abstract.en: Picture a single shaft running through a whole hall, so that every machine turns at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一根轴穿过整个车间，于是所有机器同时转动。

abstract.en: Picture an office where decisions travel along belts nobody can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，决定沿着看不见的皮带传递。

abstract.en: Picture stage rigging moving a forest while the audience watches only the forest.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台吊装移动整片树林，而观众只看见树林。

examples.en: The mill's machinery was older than any of its workers.
examples.cn: 这家磨坊的机械比它的任何工人都老。

examples.en: Agricultural machinery changed the size of the average field.
examples.cn: 农业机械改变了普通田块的大小。

examples.en: Reform required changing the machinery, not just the minister.
examples.cn: 改革需要更换机构本身，而不只是换部长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马（ma）先（chine）瑞（ry）」——马先拉动的这一整套东西，就是机械

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置」→ 拉丁 machina → 法语 machine → 英语 machine；加集合词尾 -ery（法语 -erie）构成 machinery，指成套机器，后引申指机构与运作体系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from machines as a body to the parts inside one, then to organisational apparatus, processes, farm equipment, stage rigging, abstract systems and site equipment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从成套机器出发，走向单台机器内部部件，再到组织机构、流程、农业装备、舞台吊装、抽象体系与工地设备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of machines coupled to one shaft, belts turning together until the floor trembles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排机器接到同一根轴上，皮带一齐转动，地板微微发颤。

branches.en: EQUIPMENT CLASSES: machines in general, farm equipment, and heavy site plant.
branches.cn: 设备类别：泛指的机器、农业装备，以及工地重型设备。

branches.en: INNER PARTS: the set of parts that makes one device move.
branches.cn: 内部部件：使单台装置运动的那组零件。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL APPARATUS: offices, staff and procedures that keep an organisation running.
branches.cn: 机构装置：维持组织运转的部门、人员与程序。

branches.en: PROCESS AS SYSTEM: regular steps that can be described and rearranged.
branches.cn: 作为系统的流程：可被描述与重排的规律步骤。

branches.en: HIDDEN AND VAST: stage rigging behind a curtain, and the mechanism of war or law.

definition_en: suffering from a serious mental illness, extremely angry in everyday speech, wildly enthusiastic, or foolish beyond reason
core_image: 一个人对着空椅子认真争辩，眼里的世界与旁人看到的完全不同
scene: 夜里的急诊走廊上，一位老人对着空气大声争辩，护士轻声请来值班医生。The old man had gone mad and kept arguing with people who were not there.
sceneCN: 这里 mad 是「精神失常的、发疯的」（第 1 个义项：神志不清）；句意为老人已经疯了，一直跟并不存在的人争论。图中可辨识物件：急诊走廊的灯、护士站、病历夹。

pos.zh: 发疯的；精神失常的；生气的；狂热的；愚蠢的

collocations.zh: 彻底疯了；疯得不可理喻

derivatives.zh: 由 mad 加 -ness 构成，义为「疯狂；精神失常」
由 mad 加 -ly 构成，义为「疯狂地；非正式口语中作『极其』」
由 mad 与 man 复合，义为「疯子；失去理智的男人」

senses.title: Mentally ill and out of touch with reality
senses.definition: suffering from a serious mental illness, so that the person cannot think or behave as others do
senses.definitionCN: 患有严重精神疾病，思考和举止与常人不同
senses.example: The old man had been declared mad and could no longer live alone.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老人已被判定精神失常，再也不能独自生活。
senses.why: Old English gemǣd described a mind that had been altered out of its proper state, so illness of the mind is the oldest recorded sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gemǣd 描述的是神志被改变、脱离正常状态，所以「心智患病」是这个词最早的记录义项。

senses.title: Very angry
senses.definition: extremely annoyed about something, in everyday informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中因某事而极为恼火
senses.example: She was mad at me for forgetting her birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为我不记得她的生日而生我的气。
senses.why: Anger was pictured as a passing disturbance of the mind, and the word for a disordered mind slid into the word for a hot temper.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被想象成心智一时的失序，于是那个表示「头脑不正常」的词便滑向了「火气上来」这层意思。

senses.title: Wildly enthusiastic
senses.definition: so enthusiastic about someone or something that ordinary caution disappears
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物极为热衷，连平常的谨慎都没有了
senses.example: He is mad about vintage motorcycles and spends every weekend in the garage.
senses.exampleCN: 他痴迷老式摩托车，每个周末都泡在车库里。
senses.why: Enthusiasm that sweeps away caution looks like the same loss of control, so the word moved from illness and anger to passion.
senses.whyCN: 那种把谨慎一扫而空的热情，看上去是同一种失控，于是这个词从疾病、愤怒又走到了迷恋。

senses.title: Foolish and ill judged
senses.definition: wildly foolish, used of plans or actions that no sensible person would attempt
senses.definitionCN: 极其愚蠢的，用于形容任何明白人都不会尝试的计划或举动
senses.example: Crossing the river in that storm was a mad thing to do.
senses.exampleCN: 在那样一场暴风雨里过河，是件极其愚蠢的事。
senses.why: Before it named illness, the word already meant foolish, so poor judgement remains the quiet base under every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 在指疾病之前，这个词早已表示「愚蠢」，所以「判断力差」一直是后来各义项底下沉默的底色。

intro.en: Mad is an Old English word for a disordered mind; its later senses of anger and passion grew from that base, and its deeper root is debated.
intro.cn: mad 是古英语中表示「神志失常」的词；后来「愤怒」与「痴迷」的意思都从这个底子长出来，更早的语源仍有争论。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic adjective, usually taken to mean changed or altered, and often explained as a mind shifted out of its normal state; the exact formation is uncertain.
items.cn: 一个重构的日耳曼语形容词，一般认为意为「被改变的」，常被解释为神志偏出了正常状态；确切构成仍不确定。

items.en: Gemǣd is recorded in Old English for foolish and insane, and the ge- prefix gathers the word into a completed state.
items.cn: gemǣd 在古英语中记录为愚蠢的、精神失常的，前缀 ge- 把词收进一种已完成的状态。

items.en: Middle English drops the prefix and keeps mad, and by the fourteenth century the word also means angrily excited.
items.cn: 中古英语去掉前缀，保留 mad；到十四世纪，这个词也指「怒气冲冲的」。

items.en: The phrases mad about and mad for come to mean passionately fond, first of people and then of pursuits.
items.cn: 短语 mad about 与 mad for 开始表示「极其喜爱」，先用于人，后用于嗜好。

items.en: Modern English keeps the medical sense, uses mad for anger chiefly in informal American speech, and builds compounds such as mad cow and mad rush.
items.cn: 现代英语保留医学义项，「生气」义主要用于非正式美式口语，并造出疯牛病、疯狂冲刺一类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives, a compound and one word that merely shares the spelling; the near group gathers words for a disturbed mind and for anger.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词、一个复合词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示心智失常与愤怒的词。

entries.definition: Wildly unreasonable or insane, in informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 非正式用法中指极不理智或精神失常的。

normalIntro.en: The word is an Old English name for a mind out of order, and its family keeps returning to illness, temper and the passions that overrule caution.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古英语给「失序的心智」起的名字，它的同族词反复回到疾病、脾气，以及压过谨慎的激情。

normal.en: Old English already had gemǣd for foolish and insane, and modern mad is that word with its prefix worn away.
normal.cn: 古英语已有 gemǣd 表示愚蠢与精神失常，现代 mad 就是磨掉了前缀的那个词。

normal.en: The Old English prefix ge- often marks a completed state, so gemǣd pictured a mind that had been changed into something else.
normal.cn: 古英语前缀 ge- 常标记一种已完成的状态，所以 gemǣd 画出的是被改换成了别样东西的心智。

normal.en: Three ordinary endings carry the family: -ness makes madness, -ly makes madly, and man makes madman.
normal.cn: 三个常规词尾撑起这个词族：-ness 造出 madness，-ly 造出 madly，man 与 mad 合成 madman。

normal.en: Mad for anger is normal in American speech, while British speakers generally say angry instead.
normal.cn: 用 mad 表示生气在美式口语里很自然，英国人一般还是说 angry。

normal.en: To be mad about a hobby means far more than liking it: the hobby has taken over the weekends.
normal.cn: 对一项嗜好 mad about，远不只是「喜欢」：那项嗜好已经占满了周末。

abstract.en: A mind knocked out of place, like a clock whose hands have been bent by a blow.
abstract.cn: 一颗被撞离原位的心，就像一只被一击打歪了指针的钟。

abstract.en: Illness, anger and passion share one word because all three are states that take over the will.
abstract.cn: 疾病、愤怒与激情共用一个词，因为这三者都是接管了意志的状态。

abstract.en: Mad is what English says when reason has let go of the steering wheel.
abstract.cn: 当理智松开方向盘时，英语就说 mad。

examples.en: The old man had been declared mad and could no longer live alone.
examples.cn: 那位老人已被判定精神失常，再也不能独自生活。

examples.en: She was mad at me for forgetting her birthday.
examples.cn: 她因为我不记得她的生日而生我的气。

examples.en: Many drivers go mad in the city's evening traffic.
examples.cn: 许多司机在城市的晚高峰里被逼得发疯。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mind out of its proper state; the senses then divide into mental illness, passing anger, burning enthusiasm and plain foolishness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是偏离正常状态的心智；义项由此分成精神疾病、一时的怒气、炽热的迷恋，以及单纯的愚蠢。

definition_zh: 夫人；女士；太太；小姐；对女性的尊称；（俚语）鸨母
definition_en: a polite and respectful way of addressing a woman, or a woman who manages a brothel
core_image: 一位被恭恭敬敬称呼的女士：礼貌的称呼指向一位体面女性
scene: 酒店的经理亲自上前招呼那位提着行李的客人。May I help you with your luggage, madam?
sceneCN: 这里 madam 是「女士、夫人」（第 1 个义项：对女性的礼貌尊称）；句意为经理恭敬地询问这位女客人是否需要帮忙提行李。图中可辨识物件：酒店大堂、行李箱、前台。

pos.zh: 名词：夫人、女士、太太、小姐；对女性的尊称；（俚语）鸨母

collocations.zh: 主席女士（对女主席的称呼）
先生或女士（不识对方时的称呼）

derivatives.zh: madam 的口语缩略形式，义为「夫人、女士」，多用于英式英语和服务场合
法语借词，义为「夫人、太太」，用于称呼说法语的已婚女性或称呼法语女教师
由同一拉丁词根经古法语进入英语，义为「女士；（英国）女爵士」

senses.title: A polite way to address a woman
senses.definition: a polite and respectful word used when speaking to a woman whose name you do not know
senses.definitionCN: 在不认识对方姓名时礼貌恭敬地称呼女性的用语
senses.example: May I take your coat, madam?
senses.exampleCN: 夫人，要我为您拿外套吗？
senses.why: The phrase originally meant my lady, so calling a woman madam places her in the honoured position of a lady.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本的字面意思是「我的夫人」，所以称呼一位女性 madam，等于把她放到受尊敬的「贵妇」位置上。

senses.title: A formal address to a customer
senses.titleCN: 对女性顾客的正式称呼
senses.definition: a formal word used by shop assistants, waiters or hotel staff to address a female customer
senses.definitionCN: 店员、侍者或酒店工作人员称呼女性顾客的正式用语
senses.example: The waiter handed her the menu and said, "Madam, the soup of the day is mushroom."
senses.exampleCN: 侍者递上菜单说：「女士，今日例汤是蘑菇汤。」
senses.why: Service speech keeps the old courtly habit: the customer is treated as a lady of rank, so the honourable title survives.
senses.whyCN: 服务用语保留了旧日的宫廷礼节：顾客被当作有身份的贵妇来对待，因此这个尊称一直流传下来。

senses.title: A title in formal letters
senses.definition: a word used in the opening of a formal letter to a woman, as in Dear Madam
senses.definitionCN: 用于写给女性的正式信函开头，如 Dear Madam
senses.example: The letter began "Dear Sir or Madam" because the writer did not know who would read it.
senses.exampleCN: 信的开头是「尊敬的先生或女士」，因为写信人不知道谁会读到它。
senses.why: When the reader's name and sex are unknown, the polite title stands in for the name itself.
senses.whyCN: 当收信人的姓名和性别都不明确时，这个礼貌称呼就代替姓名来充当称呼。

senses.title: A woman of authority
senses.definition: a word used before an official title to address a woman holding that position, as in Madam Chairman or Madam President
senses.definitionCN: 用于官职前称呼担任该职位的女性，如 Madam Chairman、Madam President
senses.example: Madam Chairman, may I present the quarterly report to the board?
senses.exampleCN: 主席女士，我可以向董事会提交季度报告吗？
senses.why: A title of respect can be attached to any position of power, so the word marks the office, not just the person.
senses.whyCN: 尊称可以加在任何有权力的职位之前，因此这个词标记的是职位，而不只是某个人。

senses.title: A haughty or self-important woman
senses.definition: a humorous or critical word for a woman who behaves as if she deserves great respect and special treatment
senses.definitionCN: 戏谑或批评用语，指举止傲慢、自认为该受特殊待遇的女性
senses.example: She swept into the office like a little madam who owned the whole building.
senses.exampleCN: 她大摇大摆走进办公室，活像个把整栋楼都当成自己家的小姐。
senses.why: The honourable title can be used ironically: giving noble treatment to someone who merely acts noble is a common form of mockery.
senses.whyCN: 尊称可以被反用：对只是装出高贵样子的人刻意使用敬称，正是一种常见的讽刺手法。

senses.title: A brothel manager
senses.definition: in slang, the female manager of a brothel, often capitalized as Madam
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中指妓院的女经营者，常以大写 Madam 出现
senses.example: In the novel, the madam controlled every room in the house and every coin in the till.
senses.exampleCN: 小说里，这位鸨母掌管着屋里的每个房间和钱柜里的每一枚硬币。
senses.why: The manager runs the house the way a lady runs a great household, so the title of household authority was transferred to her trade.
senses.whyCN: 经营者像贵妇掌管大宅门一样掌管那栋房子，于是「家宅掌权者」的头衔被转移到了这个行当上。

intro.en: Madam is a shortened form of a French phrase meaning my lady, and its root is the Latin word for the mistress of a house.
intro.cn: madam 是法语短语「我的夫人」的缩略形式，其词根是拉丁语中「女主人」一词。

items.en: Latin domina meant mistress, lady of the house, the feminine of dominus lord. It later gave Dame and dame in many European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语 domina 意为「女主人、夫人」，是 dominus「主人」的阴性形式；它后来在多种欧洲语言中产生 dame 一词。

items.en: Old French combined the possessive ma with dame into ma dame, a respectful way of addressing a lady of rank.
items.cn: 古法语把物主词 ma 与 dame 合成 ma dame，即「我的夫人」，是对有身份女性的敬称。

items.en: In speech the two words fused into a single form madame, which travelled to England with the French-speaking court.
items.cn: 在口语中两个词融合为单一名词 madame，并随讲法语的宫廷传入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English borrowed madame in the thirteenth century and soon clipped it to madam, and further to ma'am in casual speech.
items.cn: 中古英语在十三世纪借入 madame，很快截短为 madam，口语中又进一步缩略为 ma'am。

items.en: The polite senses stayed central, while the ironic use for a haughty woman and the slang use for a brothel manager grew out of the same title of authority.
items.cn: 礼貌义项始终是核心，而讽刺傲慢女性和俚语指鸨母的用法，都是从同一个「掌权者尊称」里长出来的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the whole my-lady family in several languages; the near-meaning group gathers other polite ways of addressing a woman.
note.cn: 形近组收「我的夫人」这一词族在多种语言中的形式；近义组收其他称呼女性的礼貌用语。

entries.definition: The French word for a married woman, used in English for French-speaking married women or French teachers.
entries.definitionCN: 法语中对已婚女性的称呼，英语里用于称呼说法语的已婚女性或法语女教师。

entries.definition: The French title for an unmarried woman, literally my little lady.
entries.definitionCN: 法语中对未婚女性的称呼，字面意思是「我的小夫人」。

entries.definition: A woman of rank or, in Britain, a woman awarded an honour equivalent to a knighthood.
entries.definitionCN: 有身份的女性；在英国指获授相当于骑士勋位的女性爵士。

entries.definition: The rank or title of a dame, formed from dame plus the suffix -hood.
entries.definitionCN: 由 dame 加后缀 -hood 构成，义为「女爵士的地位或头衔」。

entries.definition: A masked costume or a game tile; it merely resembles the Latin root in spelling and belongs to another word history.
entries.definitionCN: 指化妆舞会的假面斗篷或多米诺骨牌；只是拼写与拉丁词根相近，词源完全不同。

entries.definition: The clipped spoken form of madam, common in British and Southern American speech and in service situations.

entries.definitionCN: 意大利语「我的夫人」，用于指圣母马利亚，也是意大利语的敬称。

entries.definition: A general polite word for a woman, describing manners or rank rather than serving as a direct address.
entries.definitionCN: 对女性的一般礼貌用词，描述教养或身份，通常不作面对面称呼。

entries.definition: A woman in a position of authority over a household, from the same Latin root dominus.
entries.definitionCN: 掌管家务、拥有权威的女性，来自同一拉丁词根 dominus。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French phrase and the word's most common polite settings.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的法语短语和这个词最常见的礼貌场合。

normal.en: Madam is ma dame, my lady: two French words glued into one.
normal.cn: madam 就是 ma dame（我的夫人）：两个法语词粘成了一个词。

normal.en: The root dame comes from Latin domina, the mistress of a house.
normal.cn: 词根 dame 来自拉丁语 domina，即一家之女主人。

normal.en: Letters that do not know the reader open with Dear Sir or Madam.
normal.cn: 不知道收信人的信件抬头写 Dear Sir or Madam。

normal.en: Shop staff and hotel clerks keep the word alive when serving women.
normal.cn: 店员和酒店职员接待女客时至今仍用这个词。

normal.en: In speech it shrinks to ma'am, one swallowed syllable.
normal.cn: 口语中它缩略成 ma'am，只剩一个吞掉的音节。

abstract.en: Picture a curtsy in a palace corridor: the word is that bow, folded small enough to carry in your mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象宫廷走廊里的一次屈膝礼：这个词就是那个礼，被折叠得刚好能放进嘴里。

abstract.en: Ma and dame sit side by side; whenever you own something politely in French, you put ma in front of it.
abstract.cn: ma 和 dame 并肩而立：法语里礼貌地「拥有」什么，就把 ma 放在前面。

abstract.en: One title, many women: the honoured lady, the haughty little madam, the woman who runs the house behind the door.
abstract.cn: 同一个称呼对应不同的女性：受尊敬的夫人、傲慢的大小姐、门后掌管全家事务的女主人。

examples.en: Madam, your table is ready; please follow me.
examples.cn: 女士，您的餐桌已备好，请跟我来。

examples.en: The application form began with the words Dear Sir or Madam.
examples.cn: 申请信的开头写着「尊敬的先生或女士」。

examples.en: She has grown into a little madam who refuses to carry her own school bag.
examples.cn: 她长成了个不肯自己背书包的大小姐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买的母」——买了单的是女主人，恭敬喊一声夫人；或记「骂得母」——再傲慢的夫人也不敢让人骂她母亲

root: 法语 madame 由 ma「我的」+ dame「夫人」构成；dame 源自拉丁语 domina「女主人」，阴性形式对应 dominus「主人」。从 ma dame「我的夫人」到 madame 再截短为 madam 与口语 ma'am。

sensesIntro.en: The senses of madam all radiate from one respectful title: serving a customer, opening a letter, honouring an office, mocking haughtiness, and naming a woman who commands a household of her own.
sensesIntro.cn: madam 的各个义项都从一个敬称向外辐射：服务顾客、开启信函、敬称官职、讽刺傲慢，以及称呼一位自己当家掌权的女性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a respectful bow of words, my lady, offered to a woman who is treated as the mistress of the house.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次用词语完成的敬礼——「我的夫人」，献给被当作女主人对待的女性。

branches.en: THE POLITE LINE: unknown woman, served customer and unknown letter reader are all covered by the same respectful address.
branches.cn: 礼貌线：不识的女性、受服务的顾客、未知的收信人，都用同一个敬称来覆盖。

branches.en: THE OFFICE LINE: the title attaches to positions of power such as chairman or president.
branches.cn: 官职线：这个称呼可以加在主席、总统等有权力的职位之前。

branches.en: THE IRONIC LINE: honourable treatment given to someone who merely acts honourable becomes mockery.
branches.cn: 讽刺线：对只是装出高贵的人使用敬称，就变成了挖苦。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD LINE: the mistress of a house becomes the manager of an establishment.
branches.cn: 家宅线：女主人变成了某个场所的经营管理者。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: madame, mademoiselle, dame and ma'am are the same bow in other languages and shorter forms.
branches.cn: 词族线：madame、mademoiselle、dame 与 ma'am 是同一礼节在别的语言和更短形式里的样子。

intro.en: Madam is a phrase worn down to one word: a possessive and a noun of rank fused by daily speech.
intro.cn: madam 是被日常口语磨平的一个短语：一个物主词和一个表示身份的名词融合在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin domina and dominus are fully recorded; the fused French forms madame and madam follow from ordinary sound change.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 domina 与 dominus 均有文献记录；法语融合形 madame 与 madam 是由普通语音变化自然产生的。

senses.title: Supernatural power used to change events
senses.definition: the supposed power to make things happen by charms, spells or secret forces beyond nature
senses.definitionCN: 通过咒语、符咒或超自然隐秘力量左右事物的、被认为存在的能力
senses.example: The villagers believed that a curse could be lifted by magic.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们相信那道咒语可以靠魔法解除。
senses.why: Greek magos named a Persian priest who read the stars, and the craft of such a priest became the ordinary word for power over events that nature does not explain.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 magos 指波斯的占星祭司，这类祭司的技艺后来成了「支配自然无法解释之事的力量」的日常说法。

senses.title: Conjuring tricks performed on stage
senses.definition: the art of producing baffling effects by sleight of hand, hidden props and misdirection
senses.definitionCN: 依靠手上功夫、暗藏道具与转移注意，制造出令人困惑效果的行当
senses.example: Her act mixed quick card magic with a dove that vanished from a hat.
senses.exampleCN: 她的节目把快速的纸牌魔术和一只从帽子里消失的鸽子混在一起。
senses.why: A stage performer copies the effects the old craft claimed, so the same noun now names a trick that everyone knows is a trick.
senses.whyCN: 舞台艺人复制了古老技艺号称能做到的效果，于是同一个名词如今指一场人人都知道是假的戏法。

senses.title: A compelling, unexplained charm
senses.definition: a quality in a place, person or moment that seems to work on people beyond ordinary cause
senses.definitionCN: 某地、某人或某一刻身上那种仿佛超出常理、能打动人的特质
senses.example: There is a certain magic in the old market at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时分的旧集市有一种说不清的魔力。
senses.why: If magic means power that acts without visible cause, then a place that moves people without explanation can simply be said to have magic in it.
senses.whyCN: 如果 magic 指没有可见原因就起作用的力量，那么一个说不清为何打动人的地方，自然就可以说身上带着魔力。

senses.title: Wonderful and enchanting, as an adjective
senses.definition: used beside a noun for something that seems to work beyond ordinary means or feels enchanting
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词旁边，形容某物仿佛以超乎常理的方式奏效，或令人觉得着迷
senses.example: The garden looked magic under the first snow of winter.
senses.exampleCN: 初雪落下时，那座园子看起来像被施了魔法。
senses.why: Once the noun names a power that changes things, placing it beside another noun turns it into a plain adjective for the effect.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词指一种改变事物的力量，把它放到另一个名词旁边，就自然变成了描述那种效果的形容词。

intro.en: Magic is a word borrowed from the title of a foreign priesthood; it then split into a claimed supernatural art, a harmless stage act, a felt charm and a plain adjective.
intro.cn: magic 是从一个外来祭司称号借来的词；它后来分成号称的超自然技艺、人畜无害的舞台戏法、可感觉得到的魅力，以及一个普通形容词。

items.en: The word is generally traced to Old Persian maguš, a member of a priestly class who read the stars and performed rites.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词可追到古波斯语 maguš，指主持仪式、观测星象的祭司阶层成员。

items.en: Greek adopted the title as magos for a Persian priest or a wandering wise man, and the abstract craft was called magikē.
items.cn: 希腊语把这个称号借作 magos，指波斯祭司或游走的智者，而那种抽象的技艺被称为 magikē。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as magicus, and the related noun named the art itself rather than the man.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借作 magicus，相关的名词则指那门技艺本身，而不是那个人。

items.en: Old French magique carried noun and adjective into medieval Europe, and English borrowed the forms in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语 magique 把名词与形容词一起带进中世纪的欧洲，英语在十三、十四世纪借入这些形式。

items.en: Modern English keeps magic for the occult art and for the stage act, adds the figurative charm, and uses the bare noun before other nouns as an adjective.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 magic 指神秘技艺与舞台表演，加上比喻性的魅力，并把光秃秃的名词放在其他名词前当形容词用。

note.cn: 形近组收派生词与那个祭司称号的圣经复数；近义组收其他表示法术以及感官幻象的词。

entries.definition: A set of words believed to have magical power.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为带有魔力的一组词语。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the title of a foreign priest, and its family keeps returning to hidden knowledge, stage deception and the charm that needs no explanation.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起初是一个外来祭司的称号，它的同族词反复回到隐秘的知识、舞台上的障眼法，以及无需解释的魅力。

normal.en: Greek magos came from Old Persian maguš, a priest who read the stars, and the craft of such a priest became magikē in Greek.
normal.cn: 希腊语 magos 出自古波斯语 maguš，指观星的祭司；这类祭司的技艺在希腊语里成了 magikē。

normal.en: Latin magicus and Old French magique carried the word to English, which shortened the ending to magic.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magicus 与古法语 magique 把词带到英语，英语把词尾缩短成 magic。

normal.en: Magician adds -ian to name the person, magical adds -al for the quality, and magically adds -ly for the manner.
normal.cn: magician 加 -ian 指人，magical 加 -al 指性质，magically 再加 -ly 指方式。

normal.en: A magic wand and a magic trick keep the stage sense, while black magic keeps the darker ritual sense.
normal.cn: magic wand 与 magic trick 守住舞台义，black magic 守住了更阴暗的仪式义。

normal.en: The adjective use grew by putting the noun before another noun, as in a magic spell or a magic touch.
normal.cn: 形容词用法是把名词放到另一个名词前长出来的，如 a magic spell、a magic touch。

abstract.en: A word borrowed from a foreign priesthood now names both a stage trick and a real feeling of enchantment.
abstract.cn: 一个从外来祭司制度借来的词，如今既指舞台戏法，也指真实可感的着迷。

abstract.en: Magic survives because people still want a short name for effects they cannot explain.
abstract.cn: magic 之所以还在用，是因为人仍然需要一个短词来称呼自己解释不了的效果。

abstract.en: The same word covers a trick you can learn and a power you can only imagine.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指可以学会的戏法，也指只能想象的力量。

examples.en: The audience applauded as the magic began in a puff of smoke.
examples.cn: 观众在一阵烟雾中迎来魔术开场，随即鼓起掌来。

examples.en: The villagers believed that a curse could be lifted by magic.
examples.cn: 村民们相信那道咒语可以靠魔法解除。

examples.en: There is a certain magic in the old market at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时分的旧集市有一种说不清的魔力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马吉克」——马戏团里的吉克一挥手就变出鸽子；记住 magic 是魔术，也是魔法。

root: 希腊语 magos（波斯的祭司、占星师）→ 希腊语 magikē（祭司的技艺）→ 拉丁语 magicus → 古法语 magique → 英语 magic；一般认为可追到古波斯语 maguš。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a power that acts without visible cause; the senses then divide into the claimed occult art, the stage trick that copies it, a felt charm and an everyday adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种没有可见原因就起作用的力量；义项由此分成号称的神秘技艺、复制它的舞台戏法、可感觉得到的魅力，以及日常形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tall hat, a thin wand, and a white dove bursting out of an empty sleeve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶高礼帽、一根细棒，白鸽从空空的袖口里扑棱飞出。

branches.en: a hand passing over a bowl of water
branches.cn: 一只手从水碗上方掠过

branches.en: a white dove flapping out of an empty hat
branches.cn: 白鸽从空帽子里拍翅飞出

branches.en: lanterns coming on above an old square
branches.cn: 老广场上方灯笼次第亮起

branches.en: snow settling on a silent garden
branches.cn: 雪落在寂静的园子里

intro.en: A Persian priestly title, its Greek and Latin forms, one French borrowing and three English endings carry magic from a foreign caste to the stage and to a feeling in a place.
intro.cn: 一个波斯的祭司称号、它的希腊语与拉丁语形式、一次法语借入，再加三个英语词尾，把 magic 从外来的祭司阶层带到舞台与一个地方的氛围。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms magicus and magus are recorded, and both descend from Greek magos, which in turn is generally traced to Old Persian maguš.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 magicus 与 magus 均有记录，二者都出自希腊语 magos，而后者一般认为可追到古波斯语 maguš。
